nis2p.intro1: The NIS2 Directive (EU 2022/2555) is the European cybersecurity law that strengthens the protection of critical and digital services. It widens the scope of the first NIS Directive, introduces stricter security and reporting rules, and makes management accountable for compliance.

concerne.texte: NIS2 applies to medium-sized and large entities in 18 sectors: 11 sectors of high criticality (Annex I) and 7 other critical sectors (Annex II). Member States had to identify essential and important entities by 17 April 2025, then update that list at least every two years.
concerne.seuilsNote: Simplified thresholds, as presented on the current website.
concerne.exceptions: Exceptions: a small organisation can still be classed as essential or important if it is the sole provider of a vital service, or if a disruption would have a major societal or economic impact.

sanctions.part1: or 2% of total worldwide annual turnover
sanctions.part2: or 1.4% of total worldwide annual turnover
sanctions.retenu: Maximum administrative fines, whichever amount is higher.
sanctions.j1: Entities fall under the jurisdiction of each Member State in which they provide services.
sanctions.j2: Organisations operating in several countries are supervised by all competent authorities.
sanctions.j3: Entities that depend on activities located outside the EU must ensure their EU operations remain functional if those services are disrupted.

mesures.texte: Article 21(2) of the Directive sets out at least ten technical, operational and organisational measures, proportionate to the entity’s risk exposure. Tick those already in place.

fin.texte: SECIA helps companies assess their compliance, strengthen their cyber resilience and avoid penalties.
